requirements.evidence: All contract items exist: app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:22-102 (name/creating/viewingQueueId/confirmingToggle/editingQueueId/renameName/accessQueueId/managingAccess) and all 15 methods; Serve has selectedQueueId/mode/#[Locked] lastCalledTicketId/notice/callNext (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:29-61); routes at routes/web.php:59-60; all 19 lang keys in both locales (lang/en/ui.php:108-136, lang/pt_BR/ui.php:108-136). Edge cases handled: closeQueue resets nested state (Queues.php:111-121), scoped findOrFail (Queues.php:98,141,181,224; Serve.php:63), foreign/missing/uncallable queue yields no tickets (Serve.php:107-110), no per-row actions in the list (queues.blade.php:11-21), toggle uses a modal not wire:confirm (queues.blade.php:89-108). Gaps: `mode` is never validated (Serve.php:29,81) so a tampered value throws ValueError; the mode selector is labelled with ui.members_role and hardcoded English values (serve.blade.php:23-28); empty queue list reuses ui.serve_empty (queues.blade.php:22).

conventions.evidence: Follows the big ones: domain writes go through actions (Queues.php:76,141,181,206; Serve.php:81), authorization via policies in mount and domain actions (Queues.php:56, Serve.php:34), #[Locked] server context (Queues.php:23, Serve.php:21,30), sibling Blade/module style matches members.blade.php, CHANGELOG updated. Deviations: `name`/`renameName` have no #[Validate] (Queues.php:26,48) contrary to rule 1; helper `callableQueues()` is public (Serve.php:50) contrary to rule 5; no test-first tests; docs beyond CHANGELOG not touched.

security.evidence: Strong baseline: every client id is resolved scoped (`$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail(...)` Queues.php:98,141,181,224 and Serve.php:63; `memberships()->findOrFail()` Queues.php:208,215), foreign access queue discloses nothing (Queues.php:224-232), lastCalledTicketId is #[Locked] (Serve.php:30), output uses {{ }} only, rate limiting present (Serve.php:72-74,88). Gaps: `mode` is a public client-writable string with no #[Validate] and is passed to CallMode::from() (Serve.php:29,81), so a tampered value produces a 500 rather than a rejected request; several actions (toggleActive, grantAccess/revokeAccess, callNext) rely solely on the domain action for authorization instead of also calling $this->authorize.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all (only CHANGELOG, 2 components, 2 views, 2 lang files, layout, routes). Conventions require test-first and, for each Livewire action, happy path, validation failure, unauthorized-call and tamper tests; none of these exist for Queues, Serve or the Members tab change.

simplicity.evidence: Uses existing actions, policies, Blade components (x-label, x-input) and Bulma classes rather than new abstractions; render passes plain view data. Some avoidable repetition: closeQueue() resets the same six properties twice (Queues.php:111-121), create() calls reset('name') then assigns '' (Queues.php:92-93), mount redundantly sets mode='any' (Serve.php:35), and eight extra lang keys beyond the contract.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short and focused; the detail/access/toggle modals mirror the members page structure. Minor noise: duplicated reset block and redundant assignments (Queues.php:111-121, 92-93), `$queue->fresh()` passed for no visible reason (Queues.php:182), and nested role="tablist" plus anchor tabs without href (members.blade.php:6-13).

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: two new pages, their components, routes, navbar entries, members tabs and lang keys. No unrelated refactors or deleted code. The only extras are additional lang keys (queues_reactivate, queues_active/inactive, queues_grant/revoke, queues_access_title, queues_call_allowed, serve_title) that the views genuinely use.

issues.location: change.diff (no tests/ files) — app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php, app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php, app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php
issues.explanation: The change ships zero Pest/PHPUnit tests, while the project requires test-first development and, for every Livewire action, happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call and tamper tests.

`mode` is a public client-writable string with no validation, so a tampered value reaches `CallMode::from($this->mode)` and throws a ValueError (500) instead of being restricted to any/priority_only/normal_only.

`name` and `renameName` carry no `#[Validate(...)]` rule and `create()`/`rename()` never call `$this->validate()`, contrary to the project's Livewire validation convention (validation is delegated entirely to the domain actions).

toggleActive, grantAccess/revokeAccess and callNext do not call `$this->authorize(...)` themselves and rely only on the domain action for authorization, which is not defense-in-depth for a public Livewire endpoint.
`callableQueues()` is public although it is only used internally (mount/render), violating the rule that helpers stay protected/private to avoid exposing extra callable endpoints.

The mode selector is labelled with `ui.members_role` ("Role"), its `aria-label` is the hardcoded string "mode", and its options show raw English values, so this text is not translated through lang/*/ui.php as the task requires.
The empty queues list reuses `ui.serve_empty` ("No tickets waiting."), which is the wrong message for a page with no queues.
`closeQueue()` resets the same properties twice (once via `reset(...)` and again individually), and `create()` calls `reset('name')` then assigns `''`, which is dead duplication.
Two nested `role="tablist"` elements are emitted and the tabs are `<a>` without `href`, so they are not keyboard-focusable and the ARIA structure is redundant.
Only the CHANGELOG was updated; the new routes/pages are not reflected in the project docs (e.g. docs/architecture.md), which the conventions ask to keep in sync.

review.summary: The change adds a Queues management page, a Serve panel, members tabs, navbar entries, routes and both-locale lang keys, and it does correctly scope every client-supplied id and delegate writes to the existing actions. It falls short of a mergeable state because it ships no tests at all and leaves the public `mode` value unvalidated (a tampered value crashes `CallMode::from`), plus smaller convention, translation and duplication issues; hence overall 3.
